items.title: 8.3 Production and detection of plane polarized light

source_refs.note: Topic 8.3 with Fig. 8.5 and the Ponder Upon box (PDF 176-177, printed 173-174).

blocks.text: The light emitted by an ordinary incandescent bulb (and also by the Sun) is unpolarized, because its (electrical) vibrations are randomly oriented in space as shown in Fig.8.5 (a).

If unpolarized light is made incident on a sheet of polaroid (polarizer), the transmitted light will be plane polarized. If a second sheet of polaroid is placed in such a way that the axes of the polaroid, shown by straight lines drawn on them are parallel (Fig. 8.5-b), the light is transmitted through the second polaroid. If the second polaroid (analyzer) is slowly rotated about the beam of light, as axis of rotation, the light emerging out of the second polaroid gets dimmer and dimmer and disappears when the axes become mutually perpendicular as shown in Fig. 8.5(b). The light reappears on further rotation and becomes brightest when the axes are again parallel to each other.

blocks.alt: Two set-ups, one above the other, each a light beam running up to the right. (a) The unpolarized light beam, with arrows across it in all directions, passes Polaroid-1 (Polarizer), whose lines are vertical; the plane polarized light after it vibrates only up and down. It then passes Polaroid-2 (Analyzer), also with vertical lines, and goes on vibrating up and down. (b) The same, but Polaroid-2 is turned so that its lines are horizontal: No light comes out after it.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.5: Experimental arrangement to show that light waves are transverse. The lines with arrows indicate electric vibrations of light waves (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.5).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book refers to the parallel polaroids as “(Fig. 8.5-b)”. In Fig. 8.5 the parallel arrangement, where light passes, is part (a); part (b) shows the crossed polaroids, where no light passes. The figure also prints “Polariod” (and a stray “b” beside part (b)); the correct spelling is “Polaroid”, as drawn above.
This experiment proves that light waves are transverse waves. If the light waves were longitudinal, they would never disappear even if the two polaroids were mutually perpendicular.

blocks.title: Ponder Upon
blocks.text: Light reflected from smooth surface of water is partially polarized parallel to the surface.

blocks.alt: Sunlight from the top right falls on a smooth lake and is reflected to a person standing on the shore at the left. On the incoming ray, crossed vertical and horizontal double arrows; on the reflected ray, a long horizontal double arrow with only a short vertical one.
blocks.caption: Ponder Upon (PDF page 177): Light reflected from smooth surface of water is partially polarized parallel to the surface (original drawing after the textbook's picture in this box).
